name: Material / surface language
controls: What the graphics seem to be made of: the perceived physical substance of shapes, UI and type, and therefore how they catch light, cast shadows, reflect, deform and move.
question: What should the graphics feel like they are made of?
notes: Material is the substance an object is made of; texture (its own dimension) is the surface pattern or grain laid over it. Paper is a material; paper grain is a texture. A chrome object can be perfectly clean (no texture) and a flat vector can carry film grain (texture, no material). Material decides four things a prompt must specify: light response (matte diffuse, glossy specular, metallic reflection, transparent refraction, subsurface scattering), shadow character (crisp contact shadow versus soft diffuse), deformation (rigid, bendable, squashy, fluid) and motion physics (weight, damping, bounce). The print materials (newsprint, risograph ink, screen print, photocopy) are physical processes, so they are listed here as substances and again in texture as surface marks; pick the one the brief is really about. Most materials can be approximated in the browser with layered CSS gradients, box-shadows, backdrop-filter, SVG filters (feTurbulence, feDisplacementMap, feSpecularLighting) and grain overlays; photoreal glass refraction, caustics, true liquid simulation and physically based metals need WebGL (Three.js) or pre-rendered footage. Terms such as 'claymorphism', 'jelly' and 'gel' are informal design-community labels, not established material science categories. In HyperFrames every deformation (squash, wobble, drip) is a tween on the paused GSAP timeline, never a CSS animation.

options.what: Graphics with no implied substance: solid fills, no lighting, no shading, no surface.
options.looks: Solid vector fills and crisp edges; no highlights, gradients or shadows; objects are pure color and shape.
options.motion: Material imposes no physics, so motion is defined entirely by the motion language: shapes can morph, scale and rotate freely without looking wrong. Lighting and shadows never change because there are none.
options.use: Corporate flat explainers, UI animation, icon motion, Swiss and minimalist brand work.
options.vs: Paper implies a physical sheet with edges and slight shadow; flat implies no object at all. Flat UI (UI treatment) is the interface equivalent.
options.prompt: Treat every graphic as immaterial flat color: solid fills only, no gradients, highlights, shadows, bevels, blur or texture. Separation comes from color and spacing. Shapes may morph and scale freely because nothing implies physical substance.

options.what: Graphics that read as thin sheets of paper: layered, cut, folded, with a small physical thickness.
options.looks: Matte, slightly warm surfaces; crisp cut edges; soft contact shadows between stacked layers; occasional fibers or grain.
options.motion: Matte diffuse light, so no highlights move. Each layer casts a small soft shadow (2-8px) that grows as it lifts. Sheets slide, flip and fold along crisp creases; they flutter lightly and settle quickly because paper is light and air-damped. No stretching.
options.use: Handmade and craft brands, children's education, editorial explainers, paper-cutout styles.
options.vs: Cardboard is thicker, corrugated and heavier; paper grain (texture) is only the surface pattern, not the layered-sheet construction.
options.prompt: Build shapes as layered paper sheets: matte fills in slightly warm off-whites and flat colors, crisp cut edges, and a soft contact shadow under each layer (0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.12), 0 6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)) that grows with a 4-10px lift. Add paper grain at 5-8% opacity (SVG feTurbulence, baseFrequency 0.8, multiply). Sheets slide, flip (rotateY with perspective 1200px) and fold on crisp hinge lines; they never stretch or squash.

options.what: Thick brown corrugated or kraft board with visible edges and a rough, fibrous surface.
options.looks: Kraft-brown surfaces, visible edge thickness (3-6px), corrugation lines in cut edges, printed or stamped marks, torn edges.
options.motion: Heavier than paper: pieces tip, fall and land with a small thud and almost no bounce; folds are stiff. Matte light, rough diffuse shadows. Motion often stepped at 12 fps to feel handmade.
options.use: Eco and sustainability brands, packaging and shipping, DIY and maker content, stop-motion-style explainers.
options.vs: Paper is thin and light; cardboard is thick, stiff and heavy. Stop motion (production technique) is often combined but is a separate choice.
options.prompt: Render elements as kraft cardboard: fill #b88a5a with a subtle fibrous noise at 10% (feTurbulence fractalNoise, multiply), a visible 4px darker edge (#8a6440) on the bottom and right to show thickness, and faint corrugation stripes on cut edges. Shadows are soft and short. Pieces move heavily: power2.in falls, landings settle within 80ms with no bounce, and optional stepped timing (steps at 12 fps) for a handmade feel.

options.what: Cheap, off-white, slightly gray newspaper stock printed in black and dull CMYK.
options.looks: Grayish-cream paper, soft black ink that never gets fully black, visible halftone in images, slight show-through, column grids and serif headlines.
options.motion: Flat matte light, no highlights. Pages flip, crumple and fold; motion is quick and slightly jittery. Ink never glows; images pan within columns.
options.use: News and media graphics, editorial explainers, political and documentary pieces, retro print-editorial styles.
options.conveys: Journalism, urgency, history, authority of print.
options.vs: Halftone (texture) is the dot pattern itself; newsprint is the whole substrate plus ink. Photocopy is harsher, higher-contrast and toner-based.
options.prompt: Render the frame on newsprint: background #e9e4d8 with paper grain at 8%, ink #2a2a2a (never pure black) at 90% opacity with mix-blend-mode: multiply so it sits in the paper. Photos convert to coarse black halftone (dot pitch 4-6px). Layout on a column grid with a condensed serif for headlines. No glow, gradients or clean shadows.

options.what: Translucent soy-based spot inks laid layer by layer on uncoated paper, overlapping into new colors with slight misregistration.
options.looks: Two or three bright spot colors (fluorescent pink, blue, yellow) that multiply where they overlap, grainy uneven coverage, layers shifted 1-3px out of register.
options.motion: Flat, matte, no lighting. Motion often stepped at 8-12 fps; registration offsets jitter slightly per frame; layers can slide independently to show separation.
options.use: Indie brands, zines, culture and music events, editorial and illustration-led explainers.
options.vs: Risograph texture (texture dimension) is just the grain and speckle overlay; risograph ink as a material means the whole overprint system: translucent layers, multiply overlaps, misregistration. Screen print inks are opaque and thicker.
options.prompt: Treat color as risograph spot ink: pick 2-3 inks (fluorescent pink #ff48b0, blue #0078bf, yellow #ffe800) on uncoated paper #f5f1e8. Each ink layer uses mix-blend-mode: multiply so overlaps create new colors; offset each layer 1-3px from the others (misregistration); apply a speckled coverage mask (feTurbulence at high frequency, thresholded) so fills are uneven. Optionally re-jitter the offsets by 1px every 2-3 frames with stepped timing.

options.what: Thick, opaque flat inks pushed through a mesh, one layer per color, on paper, card or fabric.
options.looks: Opaque flat color layers with slightly soft or broken edges, occasional ink gaps and misregistration, bold poster graphics; Warhol and gig-poster heritage.
options.motion: Flat and matte. Colors often arrive layer by layer (as if printing), a squeegee-like wipe reveals each color; slight edge wobble.
options.use: Gig and event posters, streetwear, pop-art brand motion, campaign graphics.
options.conveys: Bold handmade graphic energy, pop-art heritage, craft.
options.vs: Risograph inks are translucent and grainy; screen print inks are opaque and flat. Halftone is often used in screen print but is a texture.
options.prompt: Render graphics as screen-printed layers: 2-4 opaque flat inks (no multiply), each color on its own layer offset 1-2px from registration, with slightly rough edges (SVG feDisplacementMap from low-frequency feTurbulence, scale 2-3) and occasional ink-gap speckles. Reveal colors one layer at a time with a straight horizontal wipe (squeegee pass) of 300-400ms each.

options.what: High-contrast black toner on white paper, degraded by repeated copying.
options.looks: Crushed blacks, blown-out whites, speckled toner noise, dark edges and streaks, skewed or stretched images; punk flyer and zine look.
options.motion: Matte, flat. Motion often stepped (6-12 fps), with each frame looking re-copied: noise and streaks change every frame; images slide as if dragged on the glass.
options.use: Punk, zine and street culture pieces, music, editorial collage, rebellious brand motion.
options.vs: Photocopy noise (texture) is the speckle overlay; photocopy as material is the whole toner-on-paper substrate with threshold contrast. Newsprint is softer and grayer.
options.prompt: Render imagery as photocopy: threshold photos to 1-bit black toner (feColorMatrix to luminance, then feComponentTransfer with a steep discrete table), on white paper with scattered toner speckle (thresholded high-frequency feTurbulence) and faint vertical streaks near edges. Step animation at 8 fps and change the speckle seed each step so every frame looks re-copied.

options.what: Smooth, hard, molded synthetic surfaces with soft specular highlights and saturated uniform color.
options.looks: Rounded molded forms, uniform saturated color, soft broad highlights, slight subsurface glow on thin edges; toy-like or product-like.
options.motion: Rigid: no deformation. Light and highlights slide across as objects rotate. Contact shadows are soft. Objects are light, so they bounce once or twice with moderate damping and click into place.
options.use: Toy-like 3D, playful tech, consumer product visualization, soft-3D icons.
options.vs: Rubber and vinyl deform and are more matte; glossy product surface is a lacquered, premium finish; clay is matte and hand-shaped.
options.prompt: Render forms as molded plastic: saturated uniform color with a radial-gradient highlight (white at 35-50% opacity, offset toward the light, falloff to 0 by 40% radius), a darker 10% shade on the far side, and a soft contact shadow (blur 12-20px, 20% opacity). Objects are rigid (no squash); they drop and bounce once (back.out(1.4) or a two-step bounce) and stop.

options.what: Matte-to-satin elastic material that squashes, stretches and springs back.
options.looks: Soft satin sheen, rounded edges, slightly desaturated color, broad dim highlights.
options.motion: Strong squash and stretch on impact (volume preserved), springy rebounds with high elasticity, jiggle on stop. Shadows compress and widen on impact.
options.use: Playful product motion, button and toggle animations, character-like UI, toy 3D.
options.vs: Plastic is rigid; rubber deforms and rebounds. Jelly wobbles for a long time and is translucent; rubber is opaque and settles faster.
options.prompt: Render elements as satin rubber: slightly desaturated fills, a broad dim highlight (white at 15-20% opacity), soft shadow. On every impact apply volume-preserving squash (scaleY 0.8, scaleX 1.2 for 60-80ms from a bottom transform-origin) then stretch on rebound (scaleY 1.1, scaleX 0.92) and settle with elastic.out(1, 0.5) over 400-600ms. The contact shadow widens during squash.

options.what: Semi-gloss soft PVC, as in designer toys and stickers, with a smooth, slightly wet sheen.
options.looks: Chunky, simplified forms, satin-to-gloss surface, saturated flat color, soft edge highlights; designer-toy or die-cut-sticker look.
options.motion: Semi-rigid: small squash on impact, little wobble. Highlight moves with rotation. Sticker variants peel, lift at a corner and slap down.
options.use: Mascot-led brands, sticker styles, collectible and toy-inspired motion, social content.
options.vs: Plastic is harder and glossier; rubber is more elastic. A vinyl sticker is flat and adds a white die-cut border.
options.prompt: Render forms as vinyl: saturated flat fills with a satin sheen (linear highlight along the top edge at 25% white), soft rounded edges, slight 5% squash on landing. For sticker-vinyl, add a 6-10px white die-cut border and a 2px soft shadow, and animate a corner peel (rotate plus skew on a corner transform-origin) before the sticker slaps down in 150ms.

options.what: Matte, hand-shaped modeling clay or plasticine with soft forms and visible finger marks.
options.looks: Rounded, slightly lumpy forms; matte surface with gentle soft shading; subtle fingerprints and tool marks; warm, saturated but chalky color.
options.motion: Deforms and holds the new shape (plastic, not elastic): pieces squash on contact and stay slightly flattened. Motion often stepped (12 fps, animating on twos) for a stop-motion feel. Soft diffuse shadows, no sharp highlights.
options.use: Friendly explainers, children's and education content, consumer apps, soft-3D icons and mascots.
options.vs: Claymorphic UI is the interface trend of inflated, soft-shadowed cards; real clay has lumps and fingerprints. Rubber springs back; clay stays deformed. Soft 3D is smoother and less handmade.
options.prompt: Render elements as matte clay: saturated but chalky fills, soft inner shading (inset box-shadow: inset -6px -8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.15), inset 6px 6px 12px rgba(255,255,255,0.3)), no specular highlight, slightly irregular edges (feDisplacementMap scale 3-4). Add faint fingerprint noise at 4%. Animate on twos (stepped at 12 fps); impacts leave a permanent 5-8% flattening instead of rebounding.

options.what: Lightweight porous material that compresses and slowly recovers.
options.looks: Very matte, porous surface with fine pits, soft rounded edges, pastel or bright color, no highlights.
options.motion: Light and air-damped: falls slowly, lands softly. Compresses where pressed and recovers over 300-800ms (slow return, no overshoot). Shadows are soft and faint.
options.use: Comfort and sleep products, playful tactile UI (pressable buttons), children's content.
options.vs: Rubber rebounds fast and overshoots; foam recovers slowly with no overshoot. Inflatable is hollow and taut; foam is solid and porous.
options.prompt: Render forms as foam: fully matte fills with a fine porous texture (high-frequency feTurbulence at 6-8%, multiply), soft rounded edges, faint soft shadow. On press, compress 15-20% in 120ms (power2.out) then recover over 600ms with power1.out, no overshoot. Falls use slow, air-damped easing (power1.in over a long duration) and soft landings.

options.what: Woven or knitted textile that drapes, folds and ripples.
options.looks: Soft folds, visible weave or knit pattern, matte or sheen depending on fiber (cotton matte, satin glossy), stitched seams.
options.motion: Drapes under gravity, ripples in wind, trails behind moving objects with follow-through. Highlights on satin slide along folds. Shadows sit in folds.
options.use: Fashion and apparel, home and bedding, textile-led brand films, reveals where a cloth pulls away.
options.conveys: Softness, comfort, craft, luxury (for silk and satin).
options.vs: Felt is non-woven, stiff and fuzzy; fabric drapes. Cloth simulation (effects) is the technique for moving it; true drape needs 3D.
options.prompt: Suggest fabric in 2D: fill with a fine weave pattern (repeating 2x2px crosshatch at 8% opacity) and fold shading via soft linear-gradient bands. Animate drape and ripple with an SVG feDisplacementMap driven by low-frequency feTurbulence whose baseFrequency or offset tweens slowly (2-3s), and add follow-through (drag, overshoot) whenever fabric moves with an object. Full cloth drape requires WebGL or pre-rendered footage.

options.what: Non-woven matted wool: thick, fuzzy, matte, with soft cut edges.
options.looks: Fuzzy, completely matte shapes with stray fibers at edges, visible thickness, muted-bright color, stitched or glued pieces; storybook craft look.
options.motion: Stiff but soft: pieces slide and pop in, no stretching, little bounce. Often stepped at 12 fps like stop motion. Shadows soft and short.
options.use: Children's content, craft and handmade brands, cozy seasonal campaigns.
options.vs: Fabric drapes and has a weave; felt is stiff with no weave. Paper has crisp edges; felt has fuzzy ones.
options.prompt: Render shapes as felt: matte fills with dense fiber noise (feTurbulence fractalNoise, high frequency, 10-12% multiply) and fuzzy edges (feDisplacementMap scale 2 plus a 1px blur), a slight thickness shadow. No highlights. Animate on twos (12 fps stepped), pieces pop in with small 3% overshoot and no deformation.

options.what: Solid wood with visible grain, from raw matte to oiled or lacquered finish.
options.looks: Warm brown tones with directional grain lines, rounded or crisp machined edges, satin finish; toy blocks or furniture craft.
options.motion: Rigid and fairly heavy: blocks tip, stack and knock with a crisp stop and small bounce, no deformation. Satin highlight moves along the grain as objects rotate.
options.use: Toy-like explainers, sustainability, furniture and home, craft and heritage brands.
options.vs: Cardboard is lighter and paper-based; wood is heavy, rigid and grained. Earth tones (color) are often paired but are only color.
options.prompt: Render forms as wood: warm brown base (#b07a4a to #8a5a33) with directional grain from a stretched feTurbulence (baseFrequency 0.02 0.4, 15% multiply) aligned to the object's long axis, rounded 4-6px edges, satin highlight band at 15% white. Motion is rigid and weighty: power2.in drops, crisp stops with at most one small 4% bounce.

options.what: Opaque metallic surfaces whose color comes from reflection: bright highlights, dark reflections, tinted by the metal (steel, gold, copper).
options.looks: Sharp contrast between bright specular bands and dark reflected areas, tinted highlights (gold, copper), crisp bevels.
options.motion: Rigid and heavy: slow, weighty easing, hard stops, no bounce. Reflections and highlight bands slide across the surface as the object or light moves, which is what sells the material.
options.use: Industrial, automotive and hardware brands, premium product reveals, trophies and badges, sports.
options.vs: Chrome is a mirror-polished extreme that reflects environment; brushed metal has anisotropic streaks. Metallic color alone (flat gold) is not a material.
options.prompt: Render metal with a multi-stop linear-gradient: dark base (e.g. steel #3a3f45), bright specular band (#e8ecef) at 35-45%, dark reflection (#1d2024) at 55-65%, mid tone at the edge; tint all stops for gold (#8a6a1e, #fff1b8) or copper. Add a 1px light bevel on top edges. Sweep the specular band across on reveal (background-position tween 800ms, power2.inOut). Motion is heavy: power3.out landings, no bounce.

options.what: Mirror-polished metal that reflects its environment almost perfectly, with extreme contrast.
options.looks: Near-black and near-white bands, horizon-line reflections, sharp specular hits, bulbous or beveled forms; Y2K chrome type and liquid-metal blobs.
options.motion: Reflections streak across as forms rotate; liquid-metal variants flow and merge (T-1000 style). Highlights move faster than the object. Shadows crisp.
options.use: Y2K and retro-futuristic styles, music and fashion campaigns, logo reveals, hype and gaming graphics.
options.vs: Metal (general) has tinted, softer reflections; chrome is a perfect mirror. Holographic foil adds rainbow diffraction; chrome is neutral. Liquid glass is transparent; liquid chrome is opaque.
options.prompt: Render chrome with hard-edged multi-band gradients: sky band (#dfe6ee to #ffffff) in the top half, sharp horizon line at 50-55%, dark ground band (#15171a to #4a4f55) below, and a thin bright rim highlight. Use hard gradient stops (no soft blends) for mirror quality; for bulbous chrome type layer an SVG feSpecularLighting pass. Animate by sliding the reflection bands faster than the object moves. Photoreal environment reflection needs WebGL.

options.what: Metal with fine parallel scratches that stretch highlights into long streaks (anisotropic reflection).
options.looks: Satin gray surface with fine directional lines, soft elongated highlight streaks perpendicular to the brushing, crisp chamfered edges; classic Apple hardware and early-2000s Mac OS X UI.
options.motion: Rigid, precise, weighty motion. Highlight streaks slide perpendicular to the brush direction as the object rotates.
options.use: Hardware and device reveals, premium tech, audio equipment, skeuomorphic UI.
options.conveys: Precision engineering, premium hardware, quiet luxury.
options.vs: Chrome is mirror-like; brushed metal diffuses reflections into streaks. Metal (general) may be polished or cast.
refs: Mac OS X brushed-metal window theme
options.prompt: Render brushed metal: base #b8bcc2 with fine directional lines from feTurbulence stretched along one axis (baseFrequency 0.001 0.9, 12-18% overlay), a long soft highlight streak perpendicular to the brushing (linear-gradient band 20-30% wide, white at 40%), and bright 1px chamfer highlights on edges. On rotation, slide the streak perpendicular to the brush direction. Motion is precise and heavy: power3.inOut, no bounce.

options.what: Clear, rigid, transparent material that refracts what is behind it and carries sharp reflections on its edges.
options.looks: See-through forms defined mostly by edges: bright rim highlights, thin dark edge lines, slight distortion of the background, faint reflections.
options.motion: Rigid and heavy-ish: no deformation. Refraction of the background shifts as the object moves; edge highlights slide. Shadows are faint and sometimes colored (caustics).
options.use: Premium product films, abstract 3D brand motion, AI and tech heroes.
options.vs: Frosted glass blurs the background; clear glass shows it sharply but bent. Crystal is faceted with dispersion. Liquid glass (Apple 2025) is a dynamic UI material with lensing edges and fluid morphing.
options.prompt: Render clear glass: near-transparent fill (rgba(255,255,255,0.04-0.08)), a 1px bright top-left rim (rgba(255,255,255,0.7)), a 1px dark bottom-right edge (rgba(0,0,0,0.25)), and a diagonal highlight streak at 15-20% opacity. Fake refraction by applying a subtle SVG feDisplacementMap (scale 8-15) to a copy of the background clipped to the shape. True refraction and caustics need WebGL. Objects are rigid; edge highlights slide as they move.

options.what: Translucent glass that blurs whatever sits behind it, with a light tint and a thin highlight border.
options.looks: Panels that show blurred color behind them, white tint at 10-25%, 1px light borders, soft shadows; the glassmorphism look popularized by macOS Big Sur and Windows Fluent acrylic.
options.motion: Panels slide over colorful backgrounds and the blurred content shifts behind them, which reveals the material; blur and tint can tween in as a panel arrives. Rigid, no deformation.
options.use: UI-led product films, app promos, glassmorphic dashboards, overlays on footage.
options.conveys: Lightness, layered depth, modern OS polish.
options.vs: Liquid glass adds lensing refraction at edges, specular highlights that respond to motion and shapes that morph and merge; frosted glass is a uniform static blur. Clear glass shows the background sharply.
options.prompt: Render panels as frosted glass: background rgba(255,255,255,0.14), backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(160%), 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.35) (brighter on the top edge), radius 20-24px, shadow 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.15). Always place colorful or moving content behind the panels, or the effect is invisible. Panels arrive by tweening from blur(0) and 0 opacity tint to full over 400ms while translating 16-24px.

options.what: A dynamic glass material that bends light at its edges like a lens, carries specular highlights reacting to motion, and morphs fluidly between shapes.
options.looks: Clear-to-lightly-frosted capsules and panels whose edges magnify and warp the content behind them, bright specular rims, shapes that merge and split like droplets; introduced by Apple in 2025.
options.motion: Shapes morph and merge gooily (a button stretches into a menu), highlights glide as elements move, edge lensing shifts over scrolling content. Movement is fluid and springy with gentle overshoot.
options.use: Apple-platform app promos, UI showcases, contemporary OS-style product films.
options.vs: Frosted glass is a uniform blur with no edge refraction and no morphing. Clear glass is rigid. The term is Apple's product name, now used generically for the look.
options.prompt: Approximate liquid glass: panel fill rgba(255,255,255,0.08) with backdrop-filter: blur(6-10px) saturate(180%), plus edge lensing via an SVG filter (feDisplacementMap driven by a radial or edge gradient map, scale 20-40) applied to the backdrop copy clipped to the shape; a bright 1.5px specular rim with a highlight arc that moves opposite to the element's motion. Morph between shapes with a gooey merge (blur plus alpha-contrast feColorMatrix) on springy easing (elastic.out(1, 0.7), 500-700ms). Chromium-only for backdrop SVG filters; fall back to frosted glass.

options.what: Faceted transparent material that splits light into sparkles and spectral color (dispersion).
options.looks: Sharp geometric facets with different brightness each, bright sparkle points, rainbow fringes at edges, deep saturated or clear body.
options.motion: Slow rotation reveals facets flashing on and off; sparkle glints pop on specific frames. Rigid, precise, slow.
options.use: Luxury and jewelry, awards and achievement moments, premium tier reveals, fantasy branding.
options.vs: Glass is smooth with no facets; crystal is faceted and disperses light. Holographic is a thin foil effect, not a solid body.
options.prompt: Build crystal as a low-poly faceted SVG shape where each facet polygon has its own flat fill in 3-4 values of one hue (plus white and near-black facets), and a thin spectral fringe (1-2px red/cyan offset) on outer edges. Rotate slowly and swap facet brightness values on the rotation so facets flash; add 2-3 four-point star glints that scale 0-1-0 over 250ms at key moments. Photoreal dispersion needs WebGL.

options.what: Translucent, glossy, gummy material with strong highlights and inner glow, like hair gel, candy or the Mac OS X Aqua buttons.
options.looks: Saturated translucent color, bright top highlight, glowing bottom where light passes through, rounded pill shapes; Y2K and Aqua heritage.
options.motion: Soft and slightly wobbly: small squash on press, quick settle. Highlight stays fixed toward the light as shapes move.
options.use: Y2K and Web 2.0 styles, playful app promos, candy-like 3D icons, retro UI.
options.vs: Jelly wobbles strongly and is more transparent; gel is thicker and glossier with less wobble. Plastic is opaque.
options.prompt: Render gel surfaces: saturated translucent fill (base color at 85% opacity), a bright elliptical top highlight (white linear-gradient 70% to 0 over the top 45%), a lighter inner glow at the bottom (radial-gradient of a lighter tint), and a darker 1px outline of the base color. Pill or rounded shapes only. On press, squash 6% and settle with elastic.out(1, 0.6) over 350ms.

options.what: Translucent, highly elastic soft body that wobbles long after being disturbed.
options.looks: Translucent saturated color with inner glow and light passing through, soft specular highlights, slightly rounded, wobbly silhouettes.
options.motion: Soft-body physics: squash, stretch and wobble with low damping, oscillating 3-5 times before settling. Deformation propagates across the shape with a delay.
options.use: Playful product and app promos, food and candy brands, toy-like UI, satisfying loops.
options.vs: Gel is thicker and settles fast; rubber is opaque and rebounds cleanly; jelly jiggles long and is see-through.
options.prompt: Render jelly: translucent saturated fill at 70-80% opacity with an inner lighter radial glow and a soft top highlight. Every disturbance triggers a damped wobble: alternate scaleX/scaleY (1.12/0.9, 0.94/1.06, 1.03/0.98, 1/1) over 700-900ms (elastic.out(1, 0.3) works), with skewX of 2-4 degrees on a 60ms delay to show propagation. Keep the bottom edge anchored (transform-origin bottom).

options.what: Opaque or colored flowing matter (paint, syrup, goo) that pours, drips, merges and splits.
options.looks: Smooth rounded blobs, glossy highlights, tendrils and drips, blobs merging with gooey bridges; can be flat vector or glossy 3D.
options.motion: Flows, drips under gravity, splashes, merges into bigger blobs and splits apart; viscosity sets the speed (syrup slow, paint medium). No rigid edges.
options.use: Transitions, brand films for beverages and cosmetics, logo reveals, playful product motion.
options.vs: Water is clear and refractive; liquid here means colored or opaque fluid. A liquid transition is a transition style; this is the substance. True fluid dynamics need simulation.
options.prompt: Render liquid with the gooey SVG technique: group blobs, apply feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 10-14 then feColorMatrix alpha contrast (values ... 0 0 0 20 -8) so shapes merge with smooth bridges when close. Add a glossy highlight arc on large blobs. Animate drips and merges along gravity with sine and power2 eases, viscosity-slow (600-1200ms). Photoreal fluid needs pre-rendered simulation.

options.what: Clear liquid that refracts, reflects, ripples and forms droplets and splashes.
options.looks: Transparent forms with strong refraction of what is behind, bright specular highlights, caustic light patterns, rippling surfaces, beaded droplets.
options.motion: Ripples spread in rings, surfaces undulate, droplets bead and run, splashes crown and fall. Caustics dance on surfaces below.
options.use: Beverages and hydration, skincare, sustainability, calming ambient loops, product reveals.
options.vs: Liquid (colored/opaque) flows but does not refract; water is defined by refraction and clarity. Glass is rigid; water moves.
options.prompt: Suggest water in 2D: ripple the scene with SVG feDisplacementMap from feTurbulence whose baseFrequency tweens slowly on the timeline (displacement scale 6-12), add caustics as a light overlay (feTurbulence with high contrast, mix-blend-mode: screen at 10-20%) drifting slowly, and droplets as small circles with a bright offset highlight, a dark lower rim and a magnified-background fill. Ripple rings are expanding circle strokes fading over 800ms. Photoreal water needs WebGL or footage.

options.what: A thin metallic foil with a diffraction pattern that flashes spectral rainbows as it moves.
options.looks: Silver base with rainbow bands, fine line or glitter patterns, crinkles on soft foil; trading cards, packaging, stickers.
options.motion: Rainbow bands sweep with tilt; crinkled foil catches flickering highlights; peeling or tilting reveals.
options.use: Y2K and rave styles, collectibles, fashion and music campaigns, premium packaging and card reveals.
options.vs: Holographic (color treatment) is the rainbow color look; holographic foil is the physical metal film, with crinkles, silver base and tilt response. Chrome has no rainbow.
options.prompt: Render holographic foil: silver base gradient (#b9bec6 to #eef0f3), overlaid with a repeating spectral gradient (pink, yellow, green, cyan, violet, 25% band width) in mix-blend-mode: color-dodge at 60%, plus a fine diagonal line pattern and sparse glitter points. Tie gradient position to tilt: as the card rotates on Y (perspective 1000px), tween background-position so bands sweep across. For crinkled foil add feDisplacementMap from low-frequency noise.

options.what: Thin plastic or rubber skin filled with air: taut, bulging, seamed and light.
options.looks: Bulbous shapes with rounded pinched seams, glossy highlights, slight wrinkles where seams meet; inflated type and puffy icons.
options.motion: Very light: floats, bobs and drifts. Inflates from flat to full (scale and pressure), wobbles when bumped, bounces with high restitution. Deflation sags and wrinkles.
options.use: Playful brand campaigns, puffy 3D type, social content, toy-like and Y2K-revival styles.
options.vs: Clay is solid and matte; inflatable is hollow, glossy and seamed. Claymorphic UI is soft but not air-filled.
options.prompt: Render inflatable forms: saturated fill with a strong glossy highlight (radial white 60% to 0), deep soft inner shading on the edges (inset box-shadow 0 -10px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.2)), thicken outlines into pillow-like rounded shapes, and pinched seam lines at 20% darker. Inflate in from scale 0.6 with pressure overshoot (back.out(2), 500ms). Idle: bob 4-8px over 2-3s sine.inOut. Bumps trigger wobble elastic.out(1, 0.4).

options.what: Fired clay with either a smooth glossy glaze (porcelain) or a matte speckled finish (stoneware).
options.looks: Glazed: smooth, milky, soft specular highlight, subtle color pooling at edges. Matte stoneware: speckled, earthy, gentle shading.
options.motion: Rigid, heavy-feeling but delicate: slow, careful motion, no deformation; shattering is the only break. Soft highlight slides on glazed forms.
options.use: Homeware, luxury and lifestyle, wellness, calm abstract 3D brand films.
options.vs: Clay (modeling) is soft and deforms; ceramic is fired and rigid. Glossy product surface is lacquered industrial; glazed ceramic is softer and milkier.
options.prompt: Render ceramic: glazed variant uses a milky pale fill with a soft broad highlight (radial white 40%) and slightly deeper color pooled at edges (inset shadow of a darker tint); stoneware variant is matte with fine dark speckles (sparse thresholded noise, 5%). Objects are rigid and handled delicately: slow power2.inOut moves (700ms+), gentle landings, no bounce or squash.

options.what: A polished, lacquered industrial finish with sharp reflections, as on premium phones, cars and appliances.
options.looks: Deep uniform color, crisp specular highlights and softbox reflections, mirror-like edges, controlled studio lighting.
options.motion: Slow studio turntables and hero rotations; light sweeps (a specular band traveling across) reveal form; rigid, heavy, perfectly controlled easing.
options.use: Hardware launches, product hero shots, automotive, cosmetics packaging.
options.vs: Matte product surface diffuses light with no reflections. Chrome is metal mirror; glossy product is colored lacquer. Plastic is glossy but cheaper and softer-lit.
options.prompt: Render glossy product surfaces: deep uniform base color, crisp rectangular softbox reflections (white bands at 60-80% with hard edges) placed on curved areas, bright 1px edge highlights, a mirror-like reflection floor fading to 0 over 30% of object height. Reveal with a light sweep: a narrow specular band traveling across the surface over 900-1200ms, power2.inOut. Move slowly (turntable rotations of 20-40 degrees over 3-4s). For a real 3D product use WebGL or rendered footage.

options.what: A non-reflective premium finish that diffuses light evenly, with soft gradations instead of highlights.
options.looks: Soft, velvety shading, no sharp reflections, subtle edge sheen, desaturated or muted colors; bead-blasted aluminium or soft-touch plastic.
options.motion: Calm turntables and slow reveals; light changes register as broad soft gradient shifts. Rigid, weighty, restrained.
options.use: Premium hardware, minimalist and Scandinavian product brands, wellness devices, audio products.
options.conveys: Understated luxury, calm, tactility, modern restraint.
options.vs: Glossy product surface has crisp reflections; matte diffuses them. Rubber is matte but elastic; matte product surfaces are rigid.
options.prompt: Render matte product surfaces: muted base color with broad soft shading (large linear or radial gradients spanning 10-15% value difference), a faint 1px edge sheen at 15% white, no specular hotspots or reflections, very soft wide contact shadow. Light changes are slow gradient shifts (1-2s). Motion is slow and weighty, power2.inOut, no bounce.
